Abstract View of Components of Computer

What Operating Systems Do

Different Perspectives

Operating systems serve different purposes depending on the context and the type of system.

User View

Users want convenience, ease of use, and good performance. They typically do not care about resource utilization.

System View

For shared computers (mainframes, minicomputers), the OS must keep all users happy. In this context, the OS acts as:

Resource Allocator: Manages and allocates resources (CPU time, memory space, file storage, I/O devices) to specific programs and users.

Control Program: Controls the execution of user programs and operations of I/O devices.

Specific System Types

  • Dedicated Systems (Workstations): Users have dedicated resources but frequently use shared resources from servers.
  • Mobile Devices (Smartphones, Tablets):
    • Resource poor.
    • Optimized for usability and battery life.
    • Utilize interfaces like touch screens and voice recognition.
  • Embedded Systems (Devices, Automobiles):
    • Little or no user interface.
    • Run primarily without user intervention.
